artworks.title: Hercules and Iolaus (Fountain Mosaic from the Anzio Nymphaeum)
artworks.description: This Roman wall mosaic, recovered in 1930–31 from the villa Sarsina Aldobrandini at Anzio (ancient Antium) and now in the Museo Nazionale Romano (Palazzo Massimo alle Terme, Rome), pairs Heracles with his nephew and faithful companion Iolaus. The two blond, nude heroes are set side by side in the polychrome glass-tessera style favoured for nymphaeum fountain decoration, an image of the inseparable bond between the hero and the charioteer who drove him to Lerna and seared the Hydra's severed necks. The mosaic is a rare monumental depiction in which Iolaus stands as Heracles' equal rather than a background attendant.

artworks.title: Heracles, Iolaus and Eros (relief on the foot of the Ficoroni Cista)
artworks.description: A repoussé and engraved bronze relief from the foot of the Ficoroni Cista, the celebrated 4th-century BC Praenestine (Etrusco-Latin) toilet box now in the Villa Giulia, Rome. The vignette shows three figures: Hercules at the right, a winged Eros at the centre, and Iolaus at the left. As Heracles' nephew and constant companion, Iolaus is here drawn into the hero's intimate circle, the small-scale metalwork demonstrating how the pairing of the two Theban kinsmen passed from Greek myth into the decorative repertoire of central Italy.
